title: Blueprint node for Hilbert 94 part 1: a norm-one unit (Hilbert 92) feeds the capitulating-ideal lemma
intent: Reduce the first part of Hilbert Theorem 94 — an unramified cyclic extension L/K of number fields of odd prime degree has an ideal that capitulates — to two project lemmas: Hilbert92 supplies the norm-one unit η not of the form ε/σ ε, and exists_not_isPrincipal_and_isPrincipal_map_aux turns such a unit into the non-principal-but-capitulating ideal; the three-line glue only unpacks cyclicity and forwards the hypotheses.

parent.name: exists_not_isPrincipal_and_isPrincipal_map
parent.statement:
theorem exists_not_isPrincipal_and_isPrincipal_map (K L : Type)
    [Field K] [Field L] [NumberField K] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L]
    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] [Algebra.Unramified (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L)]
    [h : IsCyclic (L ≃ₐ[K] L)] (hKL : Nat.Prime (finrank K L)) (hKL' : finrank K L ≠ 2) :
    ∃ I : Ideal (𝓞 K), ¬I.IsPrincipal ∧
      (I.map (algebraMap (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L))).IsPrincipal

children.name: Hilbert92
children.statement:
lemma Hilbert92 [Algebra k K] [IsGalois k K] [NumberField k] [NumberField K]
    (hKL : Nat.Prime (finrank k K)) (hpodd : finrank k K ≠ 2)
    (σ : K ≃ₐ[k] K) (hσ : ∀ x, x ∈ Subgroup.zpowers σ) :
    ∃ η : (𝓞 K)ˣ, Algebra.norm k (η : K) = 1 ∧
      ∀ ε : (𝓞 K)ˣ, (η : K) ≠ ε / (σ ε : K)
children.closed_by: almostHilbert92 (finrank k K) hKL rfl σ hσ hpodd
children.note: the norm-one unit η that is not of the form ε/σ ε, closed from the sibling almostHilbert92 (Hilbert92.lean:619)

children.name: exists_not_isPrincipal_and_isPrincipal_map_aux
children.statement:
theorem exists_not_isPrincipal_and_isPrincipal_map_aux
    [IsDedekindDomain A] [Algebra.Unramified A B] (η : Bˣ)
    (hη : Algebra.norm K (algebraMap B L η) = 1)
    (hη' : ¬∃ α : Bˣ, algebraMap B L η = (algebraMap B L α) / σ (algebraMap B L α)) :
    ∃ I : Ideal A, ¬I.IsPrincipal ∧ (I.map (algebraMap A B)).IsPrincipal
children.closed_by: refine ⟨(Ideal.span {β}).comap (algebraMap A B), ?_, ?_⟩; the ¬IsPrincipal goal closes by apply hη' (using the witness a from hβ'), the IsPrincipal goal by rw [hβ']; exact ⟨⟨_, rfl⟩⟩
children.note: the construction of the non-principal-but-capitulating ideal from such a unit, closed from the siblings comap_span_galRestrict_eq_of_cyclic (Hilbert94.lean:25) and comap_map_eq_of_unramified (Unramified.lean:40)

applicability.goal_shape: ∃ I : Ideal (𝓞 K), ¬I.IsPrincipal ∧ (I.map (algebraMap (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L))).IsPrincipal — an existence goal for an ideal with two properties, one in the base field (non-principal) and one after base change (principal), under Galois/cyclic/unramified hypotheses and a prime odd degree
applicability.use_when: the theorem is one node of a published result (here Hilbert's Satz 94) whose proof splits into two named project lemmas with self-contained statements — one producing a norm-one unit, one building the ideal from it — so the main proof is a short forward of hypotheses
applicability.avoid_when: the two obligations cannot be stated independently (the unit and the ideal construction are entangled); the child lemmas are not reusable elsewhere; or the node is not part of a documented dependency graph, in which case the split is a plain suffices rather than a blueprint node

The source documents the theorem as the first part of Hilbert Theorem 94: "This is the first part of Hilbert Theorem 94, which states that if L/K is an unramified cyclic finite extension of number fields of odd prime degree, then there is an ideal that capitulates in K."

The main theorem assembles 2 direct project lemmas (Hilbert92 and exists_not_isPrincipal_and_isPrincipal_map_aux), and the longest checked chain of project lemmas below it is 2 deep: exists_not_isPrincipal_and_isPrincipal_map → exists_not_isPrincipal_and_isPrincipal_map_aux → comap_span_galRestrict_eq_of_cyclic.

consequences: The move creates two obligations: (1) produce a norm-one unit η with the 'not a quotient' property, discharged by Hilbert92 (which needs the odd/prime-degree hypotheses); (2) turn such a unit into the ideal, discharged by the aux lemma. The glue must discharge every hypothesis of the aux lemma (IsDedekindDomain, unramified, norm-one, not-a-quotient), which it does by forwarding hσ, hη, and not_exists.mpr hη' — the last flips the ∀ into a ¬∃. Failure mode: if Hilbert92's statement changes (e.g. a different quotient condition on the unit), the not_exists.mpr flip in the glue breaks.
